constitutionalNote: This registry holds dimension and scheme definitions. It does NOT hold contexts: contexts are ephemeral and resolved (CX-P7). The engine contains none of the dimensions below — they are registered, so a tenth dimension is a registration, not a release.

algebraicRequirements.why: Deterministic: behaviour is reproducible and audit is possible. Commutative: results do not depend on middleware execution order. Associative: partial pre-merges do not change results.
algebraicRequirements.consequence: Context merge is a commutative semilattice — which is why the engine can be distributed and still auditable.
algebraicRequirements.unresolvedIsAHardStop: An UNRESOLVED conflict is a refusal, never a default. An evaluation that silently picks a winner is one whose audit trail cannot be reproduced.
algebraicRequirements.proofIsRequired: X-CX-03 — the engine is certified against these algebraic properties by proof, not review.

precedence.computedNotStored: Precedence is computed at evaluation time (CX-P6). Storing a precedence number invites drift between the stored order and the constitutional order.

dimensions.name: Identity
dimensions.statement: Who or what is acting, and what are they acting as.
dimensions.note: The acting principal and the beneficial principal may differ. Both are carried, separately, each accountable. Collapsing them into 'the user' is how delegation-based systems lose auditability.

dimensions.name: Temporal
dimensions.statement: When the evaluation occurs, and the temporal validity of everything in scope.

dimensions.name: Spatial
dimensions.statement: Where the evaluation is situated, physically and jurisdictionally.
dimensions.note: Jurisdiction is derived from geometry PLUS temporal validity — borders change, so jurisdiction is a contextual computation, never a stored attribute. This is where No Geography Lock-In is actually enforced.

dimensions.name: Regulatory
dimensions.statement: Which obligations and permissions apply in this situation.
dimensions.note: Attached through classification (Phase 005 section 8). An entity classified under a regulated taxon receives the regime from the taxon's policies. Regulation arrives with the industry taxonomy, never as platform code.

dimensions.name: Security
dimensions.statement: What the trust posture of this evaluation is.
invariants: every protected object has a posture (UCI-009)

dimensions.name: Economic
dimensions.note: Currency is a registered unit, never a hard-coded field (V-MS-01). No Currency Lock-In is satisfied because the unit is metadata resolved per evaluation, not a column type.

dimensions.name: Governance
dimensions.statement: Which authorities and policies have jurisdiction over this evaluation.
dimensions.note: An open dispute over a governing artifact may suspend its effect; this is registered on the dispute, not inferred at runtime.

dimensions.name: Linguistic
dimensions.statement: In what language and semantic frame the interaction is conducted.
dimensions.note: No Language Lock-In is structural: every label is a per-locale map on a registered artifact, never a string constant. Adding a language adds labels, not code.

dimensions.name: Reality
dimensions.statement: In what mode of existence the evaluation is taking place.
dimensions.note: This dimension is what makes digital twins and simulation first-class without a parallel platform. A simulation runs in a Reality context of 'simulated'; its events are marked non-canonical; and no entitlement, price, or obligation created inside it is effective outside it. The transition is a context value, not a separate system.

dimensions.name: Computational
dimensions.statement: What the execution fabric of this evaluation is.
dimensions.note: Registered, not privileged. Used by the Composition Engine. Nothing depends on it yet; it is listed here only because it exists in the registry.

mergeSemantics.if interval-like: intersection (the situation common to both contributions)
mergeSemantics.otherwise: conflict -> precedence (authorityRank, specificity, recency) -> tie and still conflicting -> UNRESOLVED -> evaluation refuses

bindingTable.Policy (C-16): scoped by context — without it, a policy applies everywhere or nowhere
bindingTable.Rule (C-15): antecedent evaluated in context — without it, rules fire on irrelevant facts
bindingTable.Value (C-20): conditioned by context — without it, a single global price, i.e. wrong everywhere
bindingTable.Entitlement: bounds include context — without it, rights valid in the wrong jurisdiction
bindingTable.Classification: assertions are context-qualified — without it, stale classifications enforced forever
bindingTable.Event (C-07): occurs in context — without it, unauditable, unreplayable history
bindingTable.Action (C-13): executed in context — without it, unaccountable action
bindingTable.Offer: validity is a window in context — without it, offers honoured where they were never made
bindingTable.Intelligence: bounded by policy in context — without it, autonomous action outside its authority

lifecycle.note: Durable contexts are rare and used only where a stable, repeatable situation must be governed.

security: CX-S-01 contributions are authored; spoofed contributions are refused
CX-S-02 security context participates in its own resolution — a low-trust contribution cannot elevate the security context it helped compose
CX-S-03 context records carry identity data, so their storage is governed by the regulatory dimension they describe (self-referential by nature)
CX-S-04 a simulated reality context may never be merged into an actual one to authorise a real action — the firewall between simulation and operation is a merge rule, not a separate subsystem
